Judgment:

1. The present is a complaint filed by Northern Railway under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (PFA Act), alleging that the accused persons have violated the provisions of the PFA Act and Rules.

The accused no. 1 is stated to be the salesman of Himachal Pradesh Horticultural Product Marketing and Processing Corporation Limited (HPMC) stall at New Concrose, Paharganj Side, New Delhi Railway Station, from where the food article, that is, "Ditto (Mango Drink)" was lifted for sampling.

entities.text: Himachal Pradesh Horticultural Product Marketing and Processing Corporation Limited
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Accused no. 2 is the Regional Manager of accused no.3 HPMC from which the product was supplied to the accused no. 1.

sentences.text: As per the complaint, on 24.08.2003, Food Inspector (FI) Jagjeet Singh found the accused no. 1 conducting the business at his stall and having stored "Ditto (Mango Drink)" for sale to passengers/public for human consumption in sealed tetra packets of 200 ml each.
He disclosed his identity and expressed intention to lift the sample.
Two Health Inspectors Khem Singh and Ramji Prasad were also joined as witnesses, when no public persons agreed.
The FI issued notice in Form VI and lifted six sealed tetra packs of "Ditto (Mango Drink)" as per procedure prescribed under the PFA Act and Rules.
Each sample was separately packed, fastened, marked and sealed and necessary documents were prepared at the spot including panchnama.
The price of sample was paid to the vendor.

Thereafter, one counterpart of the sample was sent to the Public Analyst (PA) in intact condition and the other two counterparts were deposited with LHA/Chief Medical Superintendent,
Northern Railway.
Vide report dated 09.09.2003, the PA found the sample to be misbranded on the ground that the label was without declaration of addition of colour.
Upon receipt of report, the LHA ordered investigation which was carried out by FI.
It was found that the food article was supplied by accused no.3 HPMC Limited.
Further, accused no. 2 was found to be Regional Manager and not one Sh. Prem Pradeep as told by the vendor / accused no.1 at the time of sampling.
After completion of investigation, sanction under section 20 of the PFA Act was obtained from the Chief Medical Director.
The complaint was then filed in the court on 08.09.2004 alleging violation of Rule 24 of PFA Rules as punishable section 7/16 of PFA Act.
3. As the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused persons were summoned vide order dated 08.09.2004.
Accused persons appeared in response to the summons.

4. Based on the PA report, notice of accusation under Section 251 CrPC was framed against all the accused persons vide order dated 17.12.2009 for commission of the offence punishable under section 7/16(1) of PFA Act, being violation of Rule 24 of PFA Rules, to which they pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.
5. At the trial, the prosecution examined two witnesses in support of its case.

PW-1 Ramji Prasad and PW-2 Khem Singh were the Health Inspectors who deposed about the proceedings conducted by the FI on 24.08.2003 and narrated the steps undertaken by the FI during the sample proceedings.
They also proved the necessary documents including the notice Ex. PW-1/A, vendor receipt Ex. PW-1/B and Panchnama Ex. PW- 1/C.
These witnesses were not cross-examined on behalf of accused no.1.
During cross examination on behalf of accused no.2 and 3, they denied that they were not present in the proceedings or that no attempt was made to join public witnesses.
6. At this stage, it is pertinent to note that no authorized person had been appearing on behalf of the complainant for a very long time.
The complainant Food Inspector Jagjeet Singh neither appeared in the court ever, nor was examined as a witness, nor was even cited as a witness.
Record shows that Ld. Counsel Sh. C. K. Sharma appeared as counsel for the complainant last on 03.03.2015.

Subsequently, on few occasions, the presence of Ld. SPP for Complainant (Ld. SPP appears in other matter under PFA Act on behalf of the complainant therein i.e. Department of PFA / Food Safety Department).

sentences.text: Technically speaking, the said Ld. SPP appearing in other cases could not have appeared in this case as he was never authorized to represent the complainant Northern Railway.

sentences.text: 2 Record further shows that Sh. Vinay Kumar, Advocate had appeared as proxy counsel on behalf of the complainant on 31.03.2016 and 21.07.2016.
On 30.09.2016, he stated that he was only appearing as a proxy counsel as he had not been authorized by the complainant department to represent it as a counsel.
The complainant was therefore granted one more opportunity to appoint an AR and to authorized any counsel to represent it.
However, on subsequent dates, neither any AR nor any authorized counsel appeared on behalf of the complainant.

When the matter was at the stage of recording of S.A, vide order dated 30.09.2016, this court also pointed out that the FI who had conducted the investigation and filed the complaint had neither been examined nor his name appeared in the list of witnesses.
The said Sh. Vinay Kumar appearing as proxy counsel sought time to take instructions in this regard.
But none appeared for the complainant thereafter.
7. As such, statements of the accused persons under section 313 CrPC were recorded on 27.03.2017 wherein they denied the allegations and pleaded innocence.
Accused no. 1 stated that he was only a servant and that the licensee was one Smt. Savitri Jain.

Accused no. 2 (also representing accused no.
3) denied the sample proceedings as they were not present at the spot.
He however stated that he was not the nominee of the company and was not responsible or in charge of the affairs of company pertaining to the labelling declarations.
They chose not to lead evidence in defence.

8. It is in these circumstances, Ld. Defence Counsel has submitted that there is nothing on record to show that accused persons were the persons incharge of or responsible to the company HPMC Limited for conduct of its business affairs.

It is pointed out that the food inspector who had conducted the sample proceedings, carried out the investigation and filed the complaint has not been examined on record and therefore, none of the investigative steps have been proved on record.
9. On the other hand, as already stated, the complainant stopped participating in the court proceedings.
Even Ld. Proxy Counsel stopped appearing.
There was no representation on behalf of the complainant despite several opportunities.
However, instead of dismissing the matter in default of appearance, this court proceeded with the matter on merits of the case as the evidence was already closed.
10. I have thus heard the arguments advanced by the Ld. Defence Counsel for the accused persons and have carefully perused the material available on record.
11. In a criminal case, the burden is only on the prosecution to prove its case against the accused beyond reasonable doubt by leading positive evidence.
This burden cannot be shifted to the accused and it has to be necessary discharged by the prosecution itself.
12. At the outset, it is not understood as to why the complainant chose not to examine the most important witness FI Jagjeet Singh at the trial.
Neither was he examined nor his name even cited in the list of witnesses filed with the complaint.
When the court pointed out this fact and gave time to take instructions, the said opportunity was also not availed and the complainant simply stopped appearing in the court.

The fact therefore remains is that neither the facts subsequent to the lifting of the sample have been proved nor the defence got any opportunity to cross examine any such witness on material particulars.

13. PW-1 and PW-2 were only the witnesses to the sample proceedings as conducted by FI Jagjeet Singh.
Both of them deposed about lifting the sample from accused no.1.

Except this, no further fact,
particularly the steps during investigation, have been proved on record through any witness.

14. In the absence of the examination of FI Jagjeet Singh, the complainant has not proved the necessary facts including the role and liability of accused no.1 vis a vis the HPMC stall from where the sample was lifted.

No investigation qua this fact has come on record during which it might had been ascertained as to whom the license of the stall was given, if copy of license was obtained, if the name of licenseee was ascertained or verified from HPMC.
Again, in the absence of any investigation having been proved, the complainant has failed to prove any material on the basis of which accused no.2 and 3 have been implicated.

There is no material to show if any nominee had been appointed by accused no.3 company as per Section 17 of PFA Act and if there was no nominee, on what basis accused no.2 had been impleaded to be the person in charge of or responsible to the accused no.3 company.
There is also no material to show how accused no.2 was assumed to be the person in charge of or responsible to the accused no.3 company merely on the basis of his taking the post of Sh. Prem Pradeep.
No relevant document in this regard has been proved on record not the relevant witness FI Jagjeet Singh examined to seek clarifications.
15. Even if the evidence of PW-1 and PW-2 is accepted, it can only established the factum of lifting of sample from the spot.
In the absence of any other witness, the necessary facts to establish commission of the offence and to attribute such offence to the accused persons, have remained not proved.
There is no witness who could depose and prove the role of accused no.1 in the HPMC stall particularly when his defence has been that he was only a servant.
The FI concerned has not stepped into the witness box to whom such a defence could be put to be admitted or denied or explained.
Similarly, there is no witness who could prove the investigative steps and to explain the basis on which accused no.2 and 3 were impleaded.

In the absence of examination of the FI, most of the relevant documents including the communication with the LHA, furnishing of preliminary report dated 29.10.2003, collection of relevant documents during investigation, depositing of proper counterpart with the PA, receipt of PA report, putting of specimens and seal impressions and even the complaint could not be proved as per law.
There is nothing to show that the FI could not have been examined by the complainant.

Failure to examine the complainant FI who had lifted the sample, carried out investigation and filed the complaint, would go to the root of the matter,
particularly when no public witness had been joined in the sample proceedings and there is no witness to prove the investigative steps and the conclusions thereof.
16. In view of this, it can be said that the complainant has created a big dent in its case and there is a wide missing link which goes to the root of the matter.

In the absence of the relevant facts to be proved, coupled with a situation where the complainant has stopped appearing to participate at the trial, the accused persons are entitled to be given benefit of doubt.

17. Having said so, in view of the inherent missing links in the prosecution case and its failure to prove necessary facts by examination of relevant witnesses, all the accused persons are given benefit of doubt and are acquitted of the charges.
However, the bail bonds of accused no.1 and 2 shall remain in force for the next six months in terms of section 437-A, CrPC.
